# Vienna 1683 – Metallurgy & materials

K = knowledge level · use = none/wrong/partial/correct · make = producibility with local means · accept = acceptance.

- **Copper smelting and bronze** [`copper_bronze`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/copper_bronze.md) — K4, use correct, make medium, accept high. Founders cast guns and bells in the city. Copper comes from Upper Hungary, where Thököly's uprising disturbs supply, and from Tyrol; tin is imported. Local: imperial arsenal and gun foundry; bell founders. Elsewhere: Neusohl (Banská Bystrica); Schwaz.
- **Bloomery iron (wrought iron, forging, carburising)** [`bloomery_iron`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/bloomery_iron.md) — K4, use correct, make medium, accept high. Bar iron and steel arrive from the Styrian Erzberg through Steyr. City smiths forge; they do not smelt. Stock in the arsenal must last the siege. Local: smiths, locksmiths, armourers; imperial and civic arsenals. Elsewhere: Eisenerz and Vordernberg (Innerberger Hauptgewerkschaft, 1625); Steyr.
- **Hardening and tempering steel** [`steel_heat_treatment`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/steel_heat_treatment.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Smiths harden and temper by colour and guard their quenching recipes. No theory of carbon.
- **Cementation (blister) steel and case hardening** [`cementation_steel`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/cementation_steel.md) — K3, use correct, make medium, accept high. Armourers and file cutters case-harden in bone and horn charcoal. Styrian natural steel is cheap and good enough that cementation furnaces are not wanted. Elsewhere: Nuremberg: cementation furnaces.
- **Blast furnace and cast iron** [`blast_furnace_cast_iron`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/blast_furnace_cast_iron.md) — K3, use correct, make hard, accept high. Cast-iron shot and bomb shells are bought in from the Alpine ironworks. None can be cast inside the walls; the garrison collects spent Ottoman balls. Elsewhere: Carinthian and Styrian ironworks; Walloon and Swedish furnaces for iron guns.
- **Smelting iron with coke** [`coke_iron`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/coke_iron.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept low. No coal is mined near Vienna and charcoal from the Alpine forests is plentiful, so nobody has a motive.
- **Puddling and rolling (wrought iron from pig iron with coal)** [`puddling_wrought_iron`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/puddling_wrought_iron.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept medium
- **Crucible steel (wootz, Huntsman's cast steel)** [`crucible_steel`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/crucible_steel.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept high. Damascus blades on Ottoman sabres are admired and not understood. Graphite crucibles from the Passau area come down the Danube, but no furnace here reaches the heat. Elsewhere: Persia and India: wootz ingots; Obernzell near Passau: graphite crucibles.

- **Alloy, tool and stainless steels** [`alloy_stainless_steel`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/alloy_stainless_steel.md) — K0, use none, make impossible, accept medium
- **Refractories (fireclay, crucibles, furnace linings)** [`refractories_fireclay`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/refractories_fireclay.md) — K3, use correct, make medium, accept high. The mint, assayers and founders buy Passau graphite crucibles and Hessian crucibles. Local potters' clay does not stand a steel-melting heat. Elsewhere: Obernzell near Passau; Großalmerode (Hesse).
- **Brass and metallic zinc** [`zinc_brass`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/zinc_brass.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept high. Brass is made by cementing copper with calamine and mostly bought as sheet and wire from Nuremberg. Zinc as a metal is a curiosity from the Indies trade.
- **Cupellation, parting and assaying of silver and gold** [`cupellation_assaying`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/cupellation_assaying.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Assaying after Ercker is court routine. During the siege Kollonitsch has church plate and confiscated silver coined to pay the troops. Local: imperial mint in Vienna; Leopold Karl von Kollonitsch. Elsewhere: Kremnitz and Schemnitz (Lower Hungarian mining towns).
- **Mercury and amalgamation of gold and silver** [`mercury_amalgam`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/mercury_amalgam.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Mercury from Idria is a Habsburg monopoly. Gilders fire-gild with amalgam and physicians salivate syphilis patients with it; tremor and loose teeth count as part of trade or cure. Elsewhere: Idria (Carniola).
- **Lead is a cumulative poison** [`lead_hazard`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/lead_hazard.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. Lead glazes, pewter and lead water pipes are everyday. Sour wine is sweetened with litharge in the German lands; the colic it causes is blamed on the wine's acidity. Local: vintners and wine taverns; potters (lead glaze); pewterers.
- **Soldering, brazing and tinning** [`soldering_tinning`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/soldering_tinning.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high
- **Pottery, kilns and fired brick** [`fired_brick_ceramics`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/fired_brick_ceramics.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. The bastions are brick-faced earth. Brick kilns lie in the suburbs outside the walls, so siege repairs use rubble, timber, earth and gabions. Local: suburban brick kilns (Laimgrube, Ziegelofengrund); Hafner (potters and stove makers).
- **Porcelain** [`porcelain`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/porcelain.md) — K1, use none, make very-hard, accept high. Chinese porcelain is a court treasure and its making a mystery; many think it is a kind of glass or shell paste. Kaolin and kiln heat are both lacking. Local: Habaner faience from western and Upper Hungary (the Habaner left Moravia in 1622) as the local fine ware. Elsewhere: Jingdezhen; Delft: tin-glazed imitations; Saxony: Tschirnhaus experimenting with burning mirrors and lenses.
- **Glassmaking and glassblowing** [`glassmaking`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/glassmaking.md) — K4, use correct, make medium, accept high. Green potash forest glass comes from huts in Bohemia and the northern forests; glaziers and lamp workers in the city only rework it.
- **Colourless and optical glass (cristallo, lead crystal, plate)** [`clear_glass`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/clear_glass.md) — K3, use partial, make hard, accept high. Venetian cristallo is imported; Bohemian huts are just learning a clear potash-chalk glass for engraving. Glass free of streaks for lenses is luck. Elsewhere: Murano; London: Ravenscroft's lead crystal (1674–1676); Potsdam: Kunckel, Ars Vitraria Experimentalis (1679).
- **Glass mirrors (tin amalgam and silvering)** [`glass_mirrors`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/glass_mirrors.md) — K3, use correct, make hard, accept high. Flat tin-amalgam mirrors come from Venice and Nuremberg at high prices. Tin foil and Idrian mercury are available; flat clear plate is the bottleneck.
- **Hydraulic lime, Roman concrete and Portland cement** [`hydraulic_cement`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/hydraulic_cement.md) — K2, use partial, make hard, accept medium. Builders read of pozzolana in Vitruvius and add crushed brick to lime for cisterns and wells. That clayey limestone burns to a water-setting lime is not understood. Elsewhere: Dutch waterworks: trass from the Rhine.

- **Papermaking** [`paper`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/paper.md) — K4, use correct, make medium, accept high. Rag paper comes from water-powered mills in Lower Austria and from abroad. The city's presses print orders and newssheets through the siege on stock in hand.
- **Preparing textile fibres (wool, flax, cotton, silk)** [`textile_fibres`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/textile_fibres.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Linen and wool are local; cotton and raw silk come through Venice and the Levant trade. Old linen is the only source of bandages and lint.
- **Tanning leather** [`leather_tanning`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/leather_tanning.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Tanners work by the watercourses of the suburbs, such as the Weißgerber quarter, all burned on 13 July. Bark tanning takes many months.
